summary: Full backend + frontend validation of Golden Pirates anti-spam re-application strategy. 15/15 pytest tests pass. UI verified end-to-end: Suivi locked chip, Admin 2e TENTATIVE badge + previous decision line, ApplyForm toasts (duplicate_active + cooldown with formatted date).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py — the x-forwarded-for parsing picks split(',')[-1], i.e. the LAST hop. In a typical ingress chain the real client IP is the FIRST entry; the current logic effectively keys the IP-rate-limit on the ingress IP (same for every caller). Consider using the FIRST non-trusted value or a dedicated TRUSTED_PROXIES list. In our tests all pod/browser traffic ended up sharing the same stored IP, which still enforced the per-IP cap but means two legitimate users behind the same ingress share the daily 3-slot pool.
Admin.jsx pseudoGroups is rebuilt on every render (O(N) per keystroke of search). For >200 dossiers it's fine, but could be memoised with useMemo keyed on applications.

server.py handles both status + note updates in a single PATCH but silently coerces note to '' when the client sends null; consider validating StatusUpdate.note length (max_length) explicitly like other fields.

Admin.jsx uses non-breaking fallbacks (c.status[history.prev.status]?.label) — good — but a missing status label would still render 'DOSSIER PRÉCÉDENT : undefined' because the ?? is not applied. Minor.
